# B494 row (c): a wasi:http incoming-handler component on a post-sandbox pod-IP listener
confined: yes. pod b494-http (uid 250, sandboxed=1 self-reported), node <worker-node>; profile file not readable without sudo (sha256 not recorded).

## what was needed to reach wasip2 + wasi:http (no fork, no patch)
wasmtime-go v49.0.0 wraps neither wasmtime_component_linker_add_wasip2 nor _add_wasi_http and hides the linker pointer,
and it has NO component function call API at all (no ComponentFunc/Call in component_*_feat_component_model.go).
The spike reached them with its OWN cgo in package main (CFLAGS -I <module>/build/include), calling the C symbols the
module's libwasmtime.a exports; the archive is linked by the module's ffi.go LDFLAGS. It builds its own engine/store/linker
in C; no wasmtime-go type is touched. Exported C API surface for http (nm -gU libwasmtime.a, wasmtime_/wasi_ symbols:      774):
  _wasmtime_component_linker_add_wasi_http
  _wasmtime_component_linker_add_wasi_http_async
  _wasmtime_component_resource_host_new
  _wasmtime_component_resource_type_new_host
  _wasmtime_context_set_wasi_http
There is no incoming-handler server entry point and no constructor for wasi:http/types incoming-request or response-outparam.
build/include/wasmtime/component/linker.h on add_wasi_http:
  #ifdef WASMTIME_FEATURE_WASI_HTTP
  
  /**
   * \brief Add WASI HTTP interfaces into the \p linker provided.
   *
   * This adds `wasi:http/types` and `wasi:http/outgoing-handler` to the linker.
   * Requires WASI to be added first via #wasmtime_component_linker_add_wasip2.
   */
  WASM_API_EXTERN wasmtime_error_t *
  wasmtime_component_linker_add_wasi_http(wasmtime_component_linker_t *linker);
  #endif // WASMTIME_FEATURE_WASI_HTTP
  
  /// Type of the callback used in
  /// #wasmtime_component_linker_instance_add_resource

## the component (proxy.wat, compiled at run time by wasmtime_wat2wasm)
  (component
    (import "wasi:http/types@0.2.0" (instance $types
      (export "incoming-request" (type (sub resource)))
      (export "response-outparam" (type (sub resource)))))
    (alias export $types "incoming-request" (type $req))
    (alias export $types "response-outparam" (type $out))
    (core module $m (func (export "handle") (param i32 i32)))
    (core instance $i (instantiate $m))
    (func $handle (param "request" (own $req)) (param "response-out" (own $out))
      (canon lift (core func $i "handle")))
    (instance $h (export "handle" (func $handle)))
    (export "wasi:http/incoming-handler@0.2.0" (instance $h)))

  b494: listener on the pod IP works; the guest handler cannot be invoked through the C API.
  setup:
  wat2wasm ok (369 bytes)
  component_new ok
  wasmtime_component_linker_add_wasip2 ok
  wasmtime_component_linker_add_wasi_http ok
  wasmtime_context_set_wasi + set_wasi_http ok
  instantiate ok (the wasi:http/types imports were satisfied by add_wasi_http)
  resolved wasi:http/incoming-handler@0.2.0#handle
  
  call: func_call(handle): mismatched resource types

## verdict
FAIL. The listener half works: the confined host bound the pod IP after its profile applied and answered a request from the
other node over the mesh. The handler half does not: add_wasip2 + add_wasi_http + set_wasi_http + instantiate all succeed and
incoming-handler#handle resolves, but the C API can only mint host-defined resources (resource_host_new with a u32 type tag),
and handle() rejects them: 'mismatched resource types'. The wasi:http/types resources belong to the Rust wasmtime-wasi-http
crate (its ProxyPre / hyper serve path), which v49's C API does not expose. A fork that only adds AddWasip2()/AddWasiHTTP()
(R6 as written) therefore cannot serve wasi:http incoming; outgoing (add_wasi_http = types + outgoing-handler) is all it buys.
